title: Kim2025 – 40-class beta-range SSVEP speller dataset
description: A 40-class steady-state visually evoked potential (SSVEP) brain-computer interface speller dataset acquired from 40 healthy subjects using beta-range stimulation frequencies (14.0–21.8 Hz) to reduce visual fatigue. The dataset comprises 33-channel EEG recordings (31 scalp + 2 mastoid references) sampled at 1024 Hz across 6 sessions per subject, with 240 trials total using the JFPM phase-modulation approach. This resource supports the development and benchmarking of low-fatigue BCI applications for communication and control.
methods_description: EEG data were recorded using a BioSemi ActiveTwo amplifier with 33 active electrodes (standard 1005 montage) at 1024 Hz sampling rate. Stimuli were presented in a 5×8 matrix on a 120 Hz monitor using JFPM visual flicker with 40 target frequencies spanning 14.0–21.8 Hz (0.2 Hz step) and 0.5π phase differences between adjacent stimuli. Each trial consisted of 1.5 s rest, 0.5 s cue, and 5.0 s SSVEP stimulation. Epochs were stored spanning [−2000, 5000] ms relative to stimulus onset with the event marker at stimulus onset (sample 2048).
